sections.label: Global city connectivity contribution
sections.summary: They ensure attractiveness as a global city, facilitating flows of people, goods, services and ideas, contributing about 13% of GDP and over 330,000 jobs.

sentences.text: They contribute about 13% of our GDP and more than 330,000 jobs.

sections.label: Public transport mode share targets
sections.summary: Singapore has laid foundations for a reliable, convenient and affordable public transport system, aiming for three in four commuters by 2030 and at least 85% by the 2050s.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Within Singapore, we have laid the foundations for a public transport system that is reliable, convenient and affordable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We aim to have three out of four commuters take public transport as their main mode of travel by 2030 and at least 85% by the 2050s.

sections.label: Airport and seaport capacity projects
sections.summary: Changi Airport Terminal 4 and Jewel Changi Airport are on track for 2017 and 2019, while Pasir Panjang Terminal Phases 3 and 4 will grow seaport capacity over 40% by end-2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Changi Airport Terminal 4 and Jewel Changi Airport are on track to commence operations in 2017 and 2019 respectively, while Pasir Panjang Terminal Phases 3 and 4 will grow our seaport capacity by more than 40% come end-2017.

sections.label: Public transport capital expenditure
sections.summary: The Government is investing heavily in public transport, with a projected $36 billion in capital expenditure in the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: The Government is investing heavily in public transport, with a projected $36 billion in capital expenditure in the next five years.

sections.label: Safer streets and connectivity plans
sections.summary: Aiming for zero road fatalities, plans include silver and school zones, a reconfigured North-South Corridor, and restoring Bencoolen Street with pedestrian and cycling paths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: Our aspiration is also motivated by the desire for safer streets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We can go a long way towards a future of zero road fatalities by designing streets for the more vulnerable users – children, the elderly and other pedestrians – rather than cars.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: To this end, we plan to have more "silver zones" and "school zones" that allow the elderly and vulnerable to move about safely.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: For longer distance connectivity, we will reconfigure the planned North-South Expressway to be part of a "North-South Corridor" that will include express bus lanes and a cycling trunk route to the city.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
sentences.text: We will restore Bencoolen Street, upon completion of the Downtown Line, with wide pedestrian paths and a dedicated cycling lane to connect to Rochor Canal and Bukit Timah to the north and to the city centre to the south, amongst other cycling connectivity improvements like the Queenstown-City Link and the Bishan-Kallang Link.
